function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
I don’t have direct access to a reverse‑geocoding service from within this environment, so I can’t pull the address for you in real time.  
However, you can easily get the address yourself using a public geocoding API. Here are a couple of common options:

| Service | Endpoint | Example Request | Notes |
|---------|----------|-----------------|-------|
| **Google Maps Geocoding API** | `https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json` | `https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?latlng=37.4224764,-122.0842499&key=YOUR_API_KEY` | Requires an API key (free tier available). |
| **OpenStreetMap Nominatim** | `https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse` | `https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse?format=jsonv2&lat=37.4224764&lon=-122.0842499` | No key required, but you must respect the usage policy (no heavy traffic, include a `User-Agent`). |
| **LocationIQ** | `https://us1.locationiq.com/v1/reverse.php` | `https://us1.locationiq.com/v1/reverse.php?key=YOUR_API_KEY&lat=37.4224764&lon=-122.0842499&format=json` | Free tier available, requires key. |

### Quick Test with Nominatim

If you just want to try it out quickly, open your browser and paste the following URL:

```
https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse?format=jsonv2&lat=37.4224764&lon=-122.0842499
```

You should see a JSON response that includes fields like `display_name`, `address`, etc. For example, the `display_name` might look something like:

```
"1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, Santa Clara County, California, 94043, United States"
```

### Using the Google Maps API (if you have a key)

```bash
curl "https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?latlng=37.4224764,-122.0842499&key=YOUR_API_KEY"
```

The response will contain an `address_components` array and a `formatted_address` field.

---

If you’d like me to help you parse the JSON response or extract specific address components, just let me know!
